As of 200 PM Tuesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1... Heat Advisory in effect until 8 PM tonight for the 
southern Coastal Plain. 

Central NC has been void of mid/high clouds from the waves of MCS's 
rippling through the Ohio Valley and Mid-Atlantic. Although flow 
just above the surface has been north-northwesterly via regional VWP 
data and 12z RAOB's earlier this morning, a persistent surface 
trough draped from central VA into the western Piedmont west of CLT 
has allowed generally westerly flow to continue at the surface. 12z 
RAOB data also shows a 6-12m increase in morning low-lvl thicknesses 
which will support 2 to 4 degree increase in afternoon temps 
compared to yesterday, yielding highs in the mid/upper 90s. 

In combination with dew points remaining in the mid 70s through peak 
heating across the eastern Sandhills and southern Coastal Plain, 
several hours of heat index values of > 105 are expected. Elsewhere, 
a slight reduction in dew points into the upper 60s will curb heat 
indices a bit and range from around 100 in the Triad up to 105. 

Within the complex forecast pattern, there are many failure modes 
for Wed in terms of dangerous heat. The lingering cloud cover from 
upstream MCS activity over the Mid-Atlantic will be more probable 
over the Carolinas on Wed and could temper highs by a few degrees 
and prevent reaching the thermodynamic potential through the 
afternoon. This factor along with the locations of outflow 
boundaries from convection expected later today will likely keep 
temp/dew point forecast confidence low until later tonight when the 
dusts settles. 


KEY MESSAGE 2... Conditional risk for a line of damaging straight-
line wind gusts for this afternoon within a complex and evolving 
forecast.

Regional satellite and surface observations show a slowly moving 
outflow boundary laid out northwest to southeast across eastern KY 
into northwest NC, with some deepening cu extending into the eastern 
Piedmont. An upstream MCS and associated outflow boundary is noted 
diving south along the strong theta-e gradient with 2000-3000 MLCAPE 
south and west of the frontal boundary into central NC. 
Additionally, mid-lvl water vapor imagery shows a belt of drier air 
over the TN Valley extending into NC, which will work to enhance 
downdrafts through diabatic cooling. DCAPE values of 1000-1300 J/kg 
is more than sufficient to strongly enhance outflows where storms 
group together and form common cold pools. Central NC will be on the 
southern flank of enhanced west-northwest mid-lvl winds with around 
15-30 kts to work with (greatest north and east of the Triangle). 

The environment is primed for strong winds over the forecast area 
with clusters/swaths of 50-70 mph possible, however the threat is 
entirely conditional. With the lack of any synoptic forcing for 
ascent as MCV's will likely track north of the area across VA. We 
will have to rely on outflow boundaries from prior storms (upstream 
MCS activity or developing showers/storms across the eastern slopes 
of the Appalachians) to spark more scattered to locally numerous 
showers/storms. There is a potential for convective temperatures to 
be reached anywhere within central NC, however, several degrees 
warmer air-temperatures compared to the past few days with similar 
dew points will limit 0-3 MLCAPE to only around 100 J/kg (compared 
to 125-150+ J/kg over the past several days) with the added 
difficulty of dry air entrainment to overcome from initial 
convective attempts. Forecast SPC mesoanalysis data does show hints 
of 125-175 0-3km MLCAPE developing around and east of CLT where 
multiple convective attempts would be most probable.

Greatest confidence in location where damaging winds may change, but 
current expectation is across the Piedmont, especially the western 
Piedmont, where the track of outflow shifting across central/eastern 
KY is most likely, and where preceding development in the high 
terrain within the lee surface trough is possible. From the 
longitude of the Triangle eastward, a similar environment is 
expected, but may be void of much forcing mechanisms to spark 
scattered convection and tap into the damaging wind potential over 
the forecast area.


KEY MESSAGE 3... The heat and humidity will continue into late week, 
with daily afternoon chances for isolated thunderstorms. 

Hot and humid conditions will persist through late week, accompanied 
by daily chances for isolated afternoon thunderstorms. High 
temperatures Thursday and Friday will range from the low 90s in the 
northwest to the mid/upper 90s elsewhere. High dew points in the mid 
70s will yield peak heat indices in the low to mid 100s.

Relief arrives over the weekend as a frontal boundary approaches 
Thursday and pushes through late Friday. Expect isolated to 
scattered showers and storms in the afternoon and evening. Highs
